stem:
A circuit contains a power supply that provides a sinusoidal alternating input voltage *V*ᵢₙ. There is an output voltage *V*ₒᵤₜ across a load resistor *R*, as shown in Fig. 7.1.

[[fig:f1]]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the purpose of the circuit in Fig. 7.1.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead: Fig. 7.2 shows the variation of *V*ₒᵤₜ with time *t*.
parts.text:
The load resistor *R* has a resistance of 370 Ω.

Show that the maximum power dissipated in *R* is 0.22 W.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
On Fig. 7.3, sketch the variation with time *t* of the power *P* dissipated in *R*.

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the mean power dissipated in *R*.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The circuit of Fig. 7.1 is disconnected, and *R* is connected directly across the power supply.

Explain, without calculation, how the mean power now dissipated in *R* compares with the answer in (b)(ii).

figures.caption: Fig. 7.1
figures.alt: A four-diode circuit with an alternating input supply and a load resistor connected across the output.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.2
figures.alt: A graph of output voltage against time showing repeated positive half-cycle pulses.

figures.caption: Fig. 7.3
figures.alt: A blank graph grid with power on the vertical axis and time on the horizontal axis.
